source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice long questions written from Chapter 6 (PDF 117-143), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 6 (Chemical Energetics) ke poore chapter se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke long question ki shakal mein: har sawal 4 number ka hai (wazahat, equations, zaroorat ho to diagram), aur chapter ke numericals qadam ba qadam hal kiye gaye hain. Har sawal ka poora model jawab hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 Define enthalpy and enthalpy change. Explain exothermic and endothermic processes in terms of HP and HR, with one example of each. (4 marks)
(Enthalpy aur enthalpy change ki definition likhein. HP aur HR ke hawale se exothermic aur endothermic processes samjhayein, har aik ki misaal ke saath.)
blocks.explanation:
Enthalpy (heat content), H: woh energy jo substance mein us ki structure (bonds ki qisam) aur physical state ki wajah se hoti hai.

Enthalpy change, ΔH: har substance ki apni enthalpy hoti hai, is liye products ki kul enthalpy (HP) reactants (HR) ke barabar nahi hoti. Heat ki shakal mein kharij ya jazb khalis energy enthalpy change hai:
ΔH = HP – HR

Exothermic process (HP < HR): woh reaction ya physical tabdeeli jis mein heat system se surroundings ki taraf kharij ho. Enthalpy kam hoti hai aur ΔH negative hai.
Misaal: C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = –393.7 kJ mol⁻¹

Endothermic process (HP > HR): woh reaction ya physical tabdeeli jis mein system surroundings se heat jazb kare. Enthalpy barhti hai aur ΔH positive hai.
Misaal: NH₄Cl(s) + H₂O(l) → NH₄⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), ΔH = +16.2 kJ mol⁻¹ (cold packs mein istemal).

book_ref.quote: In other words, enthalpy change is the net energy

blocks.prompt:
2 What is energy of activation? Describe the energy profile diagrams of an exothermic and an endothermic reaction. (4 marks)
(Energy of activation kya hai? Exothermic aur endothermic reaction ke energy profile diagrams bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Tamam chemical reactions mein naye bonds banne se pehle reactant molecules ke bonds tootte hain. Yeh sirf tab mumkin hai jab molecules itni energy se takrayein ke energy barrier paar ho jaye.

Energy of activation, Ea: woh kam az kam energy jo reactant molecules ko energy barrier paar karne ke liye chahiye.

Energy profile diagram (Figure 6.2): energy ko reaction ki progress ke muqable mein dikhaya jata hai. Curve reactants se barrier ki choti tak (oonchai = Ea) uthta hai aur phir products tak girta hai.
• Exothermic reaction: products reactants se neeche; farq ΔH hai jo negative hai (heat kharij).
• Endothermic reaction: products reactants se oopar; ΔH positive hai (heat jazb).
Dono mein reactants ko pehle Ea energy leni parti hai, phir products bante hain.

book_ref.quote: This can be achieved only if the reactant molecules collide

blocks.prompt:
3 What are standard conditions? Define the standard enthalpy changes of reaction, formation, combustion and atomization, giving one equation for each. (4 marks)
(Standard conditions kya hain? Standard enthalpy changes of reaction, formation, combustion aur atomization ki definitions likhein, har aik ki aik equation ke saath.)
blocks.explanation:
Substance ki enthalpy physical state, pressure aur temperature par depend karti hai, is liye durust muqable ke liye ΔH standard conditions par naapa jata hai: temperature 25 °C (298 K) aur pressure 1 atm (101 kPa). Element ki standard state 298 K aur 1 atm par us ki sab se mustahkam shakal hai (carbon: graphite).

Standard enthalpy of reaction: jab stoichiometric miqdaar mein reactants apni standard states mein standard conditions par poori tarah react kar ke products banayein to enthalpy change.
H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(l), ΔHr = –286 kJ mol⁻¹

Standard enthalpy change of formation: jab standard conditions par aik mole compound apne elements se bane (exothermic ya endothermic; standard state mein element ke liye zero).
C(s) + 2H₂(g) → CH₄(g), ΔH°f = –74.8 kJ mol⁻¹

Standard enthalpy change of combustion: jab aik mole substance standard conditions par zyada oxygen mein poori tarah jale (hamesha exothermic).
C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l), ΔH°c = –1368 kJ mol⁻¹

Standard enthalpy change of atomization: jab standard conditions par element se aik mole gaseous atoms banein.
½H₂(g) → H(g), ΔH°at = +218 kJ mol⁻¹

book_ref.quote: when making accurate comparisons of enthalpy changes for various reactions

blocks.prompt:
4 Define standard enthalpy change of neutralization. Explain why its value for all strong acid–strong base reactions is nearly the same, and define first electron affinity. (4 marks)
(Standard enthalpy change of neutralization ki definition likhein. Wazahat karein ke tamam strong acid–strong base reactions ke liye is ki qeemat taqreeban aik jaisi kyun hai, aur first electron affinity ki definition likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Standard enthalpy change of neutralization: jab standard conditions par acid aur alkali ke reaction se aik mole paani bane to enthalpy change. Yeh hamesha exothermic hai; NaOH aur HCl ke liye –57.1 kJ mol⁻¹.

Taqreeban constant kyun: strong acids aur alkalis solution mein poori tarah ionize hote hain. NaOH(aq) aur HCl(aq) milane par sirf paani ke molecules bante hain; Na⁺ aur Cl⁻ aazad ions rehte hain:
Na⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) + H⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) + H₂O(l)
Khalis: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l), ΔH°n = –57.1 kJ mol⁻¹
Is liye neutralization ki enthalpy sirf ions se aik mole paani banne ki heat hai, aur tamam strong acid–base reactions mein ΔH°n –57.1 kJ mol⁻¹ ke qareeb hai.

First electron affinity: jab standard conditions par 1 mole gaseous atoms mein 1 mole electrons add ho kar 1 mole gaseous uni-negative ions banein to enthalpy change. Cl(g) + e⁻ → Cl⁻, ΔH = –348.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (energy kharij, negative sign).

book_ref.quote: When these solutions are mixed together during the process of neutralization

blocks.prompt:
5 Define bond dissociation energy. Explain exact and average bond energies with the example of the C–C bond in ethane, propane and butane. (4 marks)
(Bond dissociation energy ki definition likhein. Ethane, propane aur butane mein C–C bond ki misaal se exact aur average bond energies samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Do atoms ke darmiyan bond banne par energy kharij hoti hai; utni hi energy bond tod kar neutral atoms banane par jazb hoti hai.

Bond dissociation energy (E): kisi substance mein khaas bond ke aik mole ko todne ke liye zaroori average energy.

Exact bond energy: kisi khaas substance mein khaas bond ki energy. Same atoms ke bonds mukhtalif compounds mein mukhtalif qeemat rakhte hain kyun ke B.E. molecule ke doosre atoms se mutasir hoti hai:
Ethane, H₃C–CH₃: EC–C = 376 kJ mol⁻¹
Propane, H₃C–CH₂–CH₃: EC–C = 356 kJ mol⁻¹
Butane, H₃C–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃: EC–C = 352 kJ mol⁻¹
Yeh har aik exact bond energy hai.

Average bond energy: mukhtalif molecules mein EC–C ki average. C–C bonds ki qeemat aam tor par 350 se 380 kJ mol⁻¹ hoti hai. Amli tor par exact ki jagah average bond energies (Table 6.1) istemal hoti hain.

book_ref.quote: This is to be noted that bonds between the same pair of atoms usually have different B.E. values

blocks.prompt:
6 Explain how the enthalpy change of a reaction comes from the breaking and forming of chemical bonds. Use the formation of water as an example. (4 marks)
(Wazahat karein ke reaction ka enthalpy change chemical bonds ke tootne aur banne se kaise aata hai. Paani ke banne ki misaal dein.)
blocks.explanation:
Chemical reaction mein purane bonds tootte aur naye bante hain, is liye ΔHr bonds ke tootne aur banne se aata hai. Chemical bond chemical energy ki aik shakal hai.

• Bond todna energy jazb karta hai (ΔH = +ve).
• Bond banana energy kharij karta hai (ΔH = –ve).
In ka farq ΔH ka overall sign tay karta hai:
• Exothermic: naye bonds banne mein kharij energy > bonds todne mein jazb energy.
• Endothermic: bonds todne mein jazb energy > bonds banne mein kharij energy.

Misaal, paani ka banna: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g), ΔHr = –ve
H–H aur O=O bonds todne ke liye energy chahiye, jab ke paani ke H–O bonds banne par energy kharij hoti hai. H–O bonds banne mein zyada energy kharij hoti hai, is liye reaction exothermic hai.
Aam tor par ΔH°r = ΣER – ΣEP; maslan H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(g) ke liye EH–H = 436, EO=O = 495, EH–O = 463 kJ mol⁻¹: ΔH = (436 + 247.5) – 926 = –242.5 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: That is whether a reaction is exothermic or endothermic is determined by the net change.

blocks.prompt:
7 Describe the glass calorimeter. How is the enthalpy change of a reaction calculated from it? State its limitations. (4 marks)
(Glass calorimeter bayan karein. Is se reaction ka enthalpy change kaise nikala jata hai? Is ki hudood (limitations) bataein.)
blocks.explanation:
Banawat (Figure 6.3): beaker, stirrer, thermometer aur dheela dhakkan jo contents ko atmospheric pressure par rakhta hai. Bahar ki deewarein cotton wool se insulate hoti hain taa ke hawa se heat ka len-den kam ho.

Kaam: reaction beaker ke andar hota hai; kharij ya jazb heat temperature ki tabdeeli se naapi jati hai. Pressure constant hai, is liye is se enthalpy change ΔH milta hai.

Hisaab: saari heat calorimeter mein rehti aur paani jazb karta hai, is liye
1. q = mwater × cwater × ΔT (paani ki c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹; dilute solutions taqreeban sab paani hain)
2. q ko 1000 se taqseem kar ke kJ mein badlein.
3. ΔH = –q/n kJ mol⁻¹ (exothermic ke liye), yani ΔH = –mcΔT/n, jahan n = moles ki tadaad.

Hudood: solution ke reactions (maslan heat of neutralization) ke liye munasib; gases wale reactions (gas bartan se nikal jayegi) ya bohat garam products wale reactions ke liye istemal nahi ho sakta.

book_ref.quote: The reaction is carried out inside the beaker and the heat evolved or absorbed is measured by the temperature change.

blocks.prompt:
8 75 cm³ of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ HCl at 25.0 °C is mixed with 75 cm³ of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ NaOH at 25.0 °C in a glass calorimeter. The temperature rises to 31.8 °C. Calculate the enthalpy of neutralization (density of solution 1 g cm⁻³, c = 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹). (4 marks)
(Glass calorimeter mein 25.0 °C par 75 cm³ 1.0 mol dm⁻³ HCl ko 25.0 °C par 75 cm³ 1.0 mol dm⁻³ NaOH se milaya. Temperature 31.8 °C tak barha. Enthalpy of neutralization nikalein (solution ki density 1 g cm⁻³, c = 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹).)
blocks.explanation: Poore mixture ke liye m c ΔT se q nikalein, bane hue paani ke moles nikalein, phir ΔH°n = –q/n.

book_ref.quote: Find the enthalpy of neutralization. Specific heat of water = 4.2 J g⁻¹K⁻¹

steps: n(HCl) = n(NaOH) = 1.0 × 75/1000 = 0.075 mol, is liye n(H₂O) = 0.075 mol

blocks.prompt:
9 2.14 g of NH₄Cl (molar mass 53.5 g mol⁻¹) is dissolved in 50.0 g of water in a calorimeter. The temperature falls from 25.00 °C to 21.90 °C. Calculate (i) the heat absorbed from the water, (ii) ΔH for the dissolution of NH₄Cl (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹). (4 marks)
(2.14 g NH₄Cl (molar mass 53.5 g mol⁻¹) ko calorimeter mein 50.0 g paani mein hal kiya. Temperature 25.00 °C se 21.90 °C tak gira. (i) paani se jazb hui heat, (ii) NH₄Cl ke hal hone ka ΔH nikalein (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹).)
blocks.explanation: Temperature girta hai, is liye process endothermic hai: paani ki khoi hui heat hal hone wala namak jazb karta hai, aur ΔH = +q/n.

book_ref.quote: ΔT is the temperature change in °C

blocks.prompt:
10 Ethanol burns according to C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l), ΔH°c = –1368 kJ mol⁻¹. Taking the molar mass of ethanol as 46 g mol⁻¹ and 4.184 kJ = 1 kcal, calculate (i) ΔH per gram, (ii) the calorie content in kcal/g, (iii) the energy released by 10 g of ethanol. (4 marks)
(Ethanol C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l), ΔH°c = –1368 kJ mol⁻¹ ke mutabiq jalta hai. Molar mass 46 g mol⁻¹ aur 4.184 kJ = 1 kcal le kar (i) fi gram ΔH, (ii) kcal/g mein calorie content, (iii) 10 g ethanol se kharij energy nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Fi mole ΔH ko molar mass se taqseem kar ke fi gram ΔH nikalein, phir 4.184 kJ/kcal se taqseem karein (calorie content = –ΔH/4.184, positive qeemat).

book_ref.quote: First, we find ΔH per gram of glucose.

steps: Fi gram ΔH = –1368 kJ mol⁻¹ ÷ 46 g mol⁻¹ = –29.74 kJ g⁻¹
10 g se energy = 10 g × 29.74 kJ g⁻¹ = 297.4 kJ (ya 10/46 mol × 1368 kJ mol⁻¹ = 297.4 kJ)

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Calorie content hamesha positive likha jata hai. ΔH negative hai (heat kharij), is liye formula mein minus sign ΔH ke minus ko khatam kar deta hai: –(–29.74)/4.184 = +7.11.

blocks.prompt:
11 State Hess's law of heat summation and show its relation to the law of conservation of energy. Illustrate it with a Hess cycle having a direct route and two indirect routes. (4 marks)
(Hess's law of heat summation bayan karein aur law of conservation of energy se is ka taaluq dikhayein. Seedhe raaste aur do indirect raaston wale Hess cycle se wazahat karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Law of conservation of energy: energy na paida ho sakti hai na khatam, sirf aik shakal se doosri mein badalti hai. First law of thermodynamics isi qanoon ka izhaar hai; Germain Henri Hess ne ise enthalpy changes par lagaya.

Hess's law: chemical reaction mein kul enthalpy change us raaste se azaad hai jis se reaction hota hai, jab tak shuru aur aakhri halaat aik jaise hon.

Hess cycle (Figure 6.4): A se B banta hai
• seedha aik qadam mein (direct route), ΔHr;
• indirect route 1 se, qadam ΔH₁ aur ΔH₂;
• indirect route 2 se, qadam ΔH₃, ΔH₄ aur ΔH₅.
Raaston mein banne wale M, N aur X, Y, Z reaction intermediates hain. Hess's law ke mutabiq:
Indirect route 1: ΔHr = ΔH₁ + ΔH₂
Indirect route 2: ΔHr = ΔH₃ + ΔH₄ + ΔH₅

Ahmiyat: bohat se reactions ka ΔH calorimetry se seedha nahi naapa ja sakta, maslan CCl₄ carbon aur chlorine se seedha nahi banta; Hess's law se aise enthalpy changes nikale jate hain.

book_ref.quote: Let A be converted to ‘B’ directly in a single step, which is the direct route

blocks.prompt:
12 When 4.00 g of methane, CH₄ (16.0 g mol⁻¹), is burned in excess oxygen, 222.6 kJ of heat is evolved: CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l). Given ΔH°f[CO₂(g)] = –393.5 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔH°f[H₂O(l)] = –285.8 kJ mol⁻¹, calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of methane. (4 marks)
(Jab 4.00 g methane, CH₄ (16.0 g mol⁻¹), zyada oxygen mein jalai gayi to 222.6 kJ heat kharij hui: CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l). ΔH°f[CO₂(g)] = –393.5 kJ mol⁻¹ aur ΔH°f[H₂O(l)] = –285.8 kJ mol⁻¹ hain. Methane ki standard enthalpy of formation nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Pehle fi mole methane ka ΔH°c nikalein, phir Hess's law lagayein: ΔHr = ΣΔH°f(products) – ΣΔH°f(reactants), ΔH°f(O₂) = 0.

book_ref.quote: Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of propane.

blocks.final_answer: ΔH°f(CH₄) = –74.7 kJ mol⁻¹ (chapter ki –74.8 kJ mol⁻¹ ke qareeb)

blocks.prompt:
13 For C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) → C₂H₆(g), calculate ΔH°r (i) from enthalpies of formation, ΔH°f(C₂H₄) = +52.2 and ΔH°f(C₂H₆) = –84.7 kJ mol⁻¹, and (ii) from the average bond energies EC=C = 615, EC–C = 348, EC–H = 413 and EH–H = 436 kJ mol⁻¹. Why do the two answers differ? (4 marks)
(C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) → C₂H₆(g) ke liye ΔH°r nikalein (i) enthalpies of formation se, ΔH°f(C₂H₄) = +52.2 aur ΔH°f(C₂H₆) = –84.7 kJ mol⁻¹, aur (ii) average bond energies EC=C = 615, EC–C = 348, EC–H = 413, EH–H = 436 kJ mol⁻¹ se. Dono jawab mukhtalif kyun hain?)
blocks.explanation: (i) ke liye ΣΔH°f(products) – ΣΔH°f(reactants), aur (ii) ke liye ΣER – ΣEP lagayein; sirf badalne wale bonds ginein.

book_ref.quote: The enthalpy change for this step can be calculated by adding the bond enthalpies from Table 6.1.

steps: (ii) Toote bonds: aik C=C + aik H–H = 615 + 436 = 1051 kJ (C₂H₄ ke chaar C–H bonds baqi rehte hain)
Bane bonds: aik C–C + do naye C–H = 348 + 2(413) = 1174 kJ
Farq is liye hai ke (ii) mein in molecules ki exact nahi balke average bond energies li gayi hain, is liye yeh sirf andaza hai.
blocks.final_answer: (i) –136.9 kJ mol⁻¹; (ii) –123 kJ mol⁻¹ (average bond energies se andaza)

blocks.prompt:
14 Use bond energies from Table 6.1 (EN≡N = 945, EH–H = 436, EN–H = 391 kJ mol⁻¹) to estimate ΔH for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g), and hence the enthalpy of formation of NH₃(g). (4 marks)
(Table 6.1 ki bond energies (EN≡N = 945, EH–H = 436, EN–H = 391 kJ mol⁻¹) se N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g) ka ΔH andaza karein, aur phir NH₃(g) ki enthalpy of formation nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Reaction ko do qadmon se badlein: reactants ke tamam bonds tod kar gaseous atoms (ΣER), phir products ke bonds (ΣEP); ΔH = ΣER – ΣEP, phir aik mole NH₃ ke liye 2 se taqseem karein.

book_ref.quote: And finally calculate the heat of formation of HCl.

steps: Qadam 2: 2N(g) + 6H(g) → 2NH₃(g); chhe N–H bonds bane: ΣEP = 6(391) = 2346 kJ
ΔHr = ΣER – ΣEP = 2253 – 2346 = –93 kJ (2 mol NH₃ ke liye)
blocks.final_answer: ΔHr = –93 kJ; ΔH°f(NH₃) ≈ –46.5 kJ mol⁻¹ (chapter ki naapi gayi qeemat –45.9 kJ mol⁻¹ hai)

blocks.prompt:
15 Define dissolution and standard enthalpy of solution. Describe the three steps of solution formation and the two factors that govern the dissolution of an ionic compound. (4 marks)
(Dissolution aur standard enthalpy of solution ki definitions likhein. Solution banne ke teen qadam aur ionic compound ke hal hone ko control karne wale do factors bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Dissolution: solute ko solvent mein hal karne ka amal.

Standard enthalpy of solution, ΔH°sol: woh heat jo aik mole substance solvent mein hal ho kar infinitely dilute solution banane par jazb ya kharij ho. Yeh exothermic ya endothermic ho sakti hai:
Na₂CO₃(s) + aq → 2Na⁺(aq) + CO₃²⁻(aq), ΔH°sol = –25 kJ mol⁻¹
NH₄Cl(s) + aq → NH₄⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), ΔH°sol = +16.2 kJ mol⁻¹

Teen qadam (farzi):
1. Solvent ki intermolecular forces par qaboo pa kar solute ke liye jagah banana (solvent ko phailana).
2. Solute ko alag alag hisson mein todna (solute ko phailana).
3. Solute aur solvent ka aapas mein mil kar solution banana.
Is amal mein heat kharij ya jazb hoti hai.

Ionic compound (mazboot electrostatic forces se jure mukhalif charge wale ions) ke do factors:
• Lattice energy, jo ionic compound ke tootne ko control karti hai;
• Hydration energy, jo solute ions ki paani ke molecules se kashish ko zahir karti hai.

book_ref.quote: In this process heat is either given out or taken in.

blocks.prompt:
16 What is hydration? Explain the factors that affect the magnitude of hydration energy, with examples of the order of hydration enthalpies. (4 marks)
(Hydration kya hai? Hydration energy ki miqdaar par asar dalne wale factors misaalon ke saath samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Hydration: ionic compounds paani mein hal ho kar ions mein toot-te hain; paani ke molecules ka solute ions ko gher kar un se interact karna hydration hai. Paani ke molecules aur ions ke darmiyan ion-dipole forces hoti hain (Figure 6.5), aur ions hydrated kehlate hain.

Enthalpy of hydration, ΔHhyd: ion-dipole forces ki kashish ki energy. Yeh hamesha kharij hoti hai kyun ke ion-dipole bonds bante hain.

Factors:
1. Ion par charge
2. Ion ka size
In dono ko charge density (charge fi unit area) kehte hain. Chhote ion par zyada charge ho to charge density zyada; aise ions paani ko zyada kheenchte hain, is liye hydration energy zyada.

Misalein:
• Na⁺ < Mg²⁺ < Al³⁺: charge barhta aur size kam hota hai, is liye hydration energy barhti hai.
• Mg²⁺ > Ca²⁺ > Sr²⁺: charge same, group mein neeche size barhta hai, is liye hydration energy kam hoti hai.
Anions ki hydration energy bhi isi buniyad par samjhi jati hai.

book_ref.quote: For example, enthalpies of hydration of following ions are in the order:

blocks.prompt:
17 Define lattice energy. Explain how the charge and the size of the ions affect the magnitude of lattice energy, with examples. (4 marks)
(Lattice energy ki definition likhein. Misaalon ke saath samjhayein ke ions ka charge aur size lattice energy ki miqdaar par kaise asar dalte hain.)
blocks.explanation:
Lattice energy, ΔHlatt: jab standard conditions par gaseous ions se aik mole ionic compound bane to enthalpy change. Yeh kharij hoti hai, is liye negative hai:
Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g) → NaCl(s), ΔH°latt = –787 kJ mol⁻¹

1. Ions ka charge: ions par charge jitna zyada, lattice energy utni zyada. LiF aur MgO mein ions ki tarteeb aur size milte julte hain; asal farq charge ka hai.
ΔHlatt[MgO] = –3923 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔHlatt[LiF] = –1049 kJ mol⁻¹
Doubly charged Mg²⁺ aur O²⁻ same size ke singly charged ions se zyada kheenchte hain; zyada charge = zyada charge density aur mazboot ionic bonds.

2. Ions ka size: alkali metal halides (Figure 6.6) mein cation ya anion ka size barhne se lattice energy kam hoti hai, kyun ke bade ions kam qareeb jurte hain aur mukhalif charge wale ions ki kashish kamzor hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Let us try to understand this fact by comparing lithium fluoride, LiF, with magnesium oxide, MgO.

blocks.prompt:
18 Explain, in terms of lattice energy and hydration energy, the solubility trends of the Group II hydroxides and sulphates. (4 marks)
(Lattice energy aur hydration energy ke hawale se Group II hydroxides aur sulphates ki solubility ke rujhanaat samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
ΔH°sol lattice energy aur hydration enthalpy dono par depend karta hai (ΔH°sol = ΔH°hyd – ΔH°latt).

Group II hydroxides, Mg(OH)₂ → Ba(OH)₂:
• Group mein neeche cations ki hydration energy aur lattice energy dono kam hoti hain, kyun ke Group 2 cations ki charge density kam hoti hai.
• Mg(OH)₂, Ca(OH)₂, Sr(OH)₂, Ba(OH)₂ mein lattice energy, Mg²⁺, Ca²⁺, Sr²⁺, Ba²⁺ ki hydration energy se zyada tezi se kam hoti hai.
• Lattice energy haawi hai; ΔH°sol zyada exothermic hota hai, is liye group mein neeche solubility barhti hai.

Group II sulphates, MgSO₄ → BaSO₄:
• Sulphate ion (SO₄²⁻) OH⁻ se kahin bada hai, is liye MgSO₄ se BaSO₄ tak lattice energy thodi kam hoti hai.
• Cation ki hydration energy zyada kam hoti hai.
• Hydration energy haawi hai; ΔH°sol zyada endothermic hota hai, is liye MgSO₄ se BaSO₄ tak solubility kam hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Look at the solubility trends of group II metal hydroxides.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book correction: kitab mein sulphate ion SO₄²⁺ chhapa hai, sahi SO₄²⁻ hai; aur sulphates mein ΔH°sol zyada endothermic hone ka matlab solubility KAM hona hai.

blocks.prompt:
19 Using an enthalpy cycle, calculate the standard enthalpy change of solution of KCl from: lattice energy of KCl = –718 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔH°hyd(K⁺) = –322 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔH°hyd(Cl⁻) = –378 kJ mol⁻¹. Is the dissolution exothermic or endothermic? (4 marks)
(Enthalpy cycle se KCl ki standard enthalpy change of solution nikalein: KCl ki lattice energy = –718 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔH°hyd(K⁺) = –322 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔH°hyd(Cl⁻) = –378 kJ mol⁻¹. Hal hona exothermic hai ya endothermic?)
blocks.explanation: Cycle banayein: gaseous ions → solid (ΔH°latt), solid → aqueous ions (ΔH°sol), gaseous ions → aqueous ions (ΔH°hyd); Hess's law se ΔH°latt + ΔH°sol = ΔH°hyd.

book_ref.quote: Determine the enthalpy change of solution

steps: Cycle: K⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g) → KCl(s) (ΔH°latt); KCl(s) + aq → K⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) (ΔH°sol); K⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g) + aq → K⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) (ΔH°hyd)
ΔH°latt + ΔH°sol = ΔH°hyd, is liye ΔH°sol = ΔH°hyd – ΔH°latt
blocks.final_answer: ΔH°sol(KCl) = +18 kJ mol⁻¹: endothermic (Table 6.2 mein 17.8 kJ mol⁻¹)

blocks.prompt:
20 Why is the Born-Haber cycle needed? Describe the Born-Haber cycle for sodium chloride, naming each step and writing the relation used to find ΔH°latt. (4 marks)
(Born-Haber cycle ki zaroorat kyun hai? Sodium chloride ka Born-Haber cycle bayan karein, har qadam ka naam aur ΔH°latt nikalne ka taaluq likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Zaroorat: compound ki lattice energy aik seedhe tajurbe se maloom nahi ho sakti. Yeh kai tajurbati data se aik energy cycle, Born-Haber cycle, ke zariye nikali jati hai jo Hess's law ka itlaaq hai.

Energy triangle: Na(s) + ½Cl₂(g) → Na⁺Cl⁻(s) seedha (ΔH°f, calorimeter mein naapa jata hai), ya pehle gaseous ions Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g) (ΔHx) aur phir solid (ΔH°latt):
ΔHx + ΔH°latt = ΔH°f

ΔHx ke marahil (Figure 6.9):
1. Sodium ki atomization: Na(s) → Na(g), ΔH°at(Na)
2. Sodium ki first ionization: Na(g) → Na⁺(g) + e⁻, ΔH°i1(Na)
3. Chlorine ki atomization: ½Cl₂(g) → Cl(g), ΔH°at(Cl)
4. Chlorine ki first electron affinity: Cl(g) + e⁻ → Cl⁻(g), ΔH°ea1(Cl)
ΔHx = ΔH°at(Na) + ΔH°i1(Na) + ΔH°at(Cl) + ΔH°ea1(Cl) = 376 kJ mol⁻¹
5. Gaseous ions se solid: Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g) → NaCl(s), ΔH°latt

Is liye NaCl ke liye ΔH°latt = ΔH°f – ΔHx = –787 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: The above energy triangle has been extended to show the various stages involved in finding ΔHx.

blocks.prompt:
22 Define entropy. Explain entropy in terms of diffusion and the number of ways of arrangement of molecules in two connected jars. (4 marks)
(Entropy ki definition likhein. Do jure hue jars mein molecules ki diffusion aur tarteeb ke tareeqon ke hawale se entropy samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Entropy: is baat ka paimana ke khaas temperature par system mein energy kitne tareeqon se bant sakti hai. Energy zyada tareeqon se bante to system zyada mustahkam hota hai. Entropy randomness ya disorder ka bhi paimana hai: zyada disorder, zyada entropy.

Diffusion model (Figure 6.10): bhaap ke molecules ittefaq se phailte hain. Molecules wala jar A khaali jar B se jura hai; stopcock kholne par har molecule kisi bhi jar mein ho sakta hai.
• A mein molecules = 3, jars = 2: tarteebein = 2³ = 8
• 5 molecules ke saath: 2⁵ = 32
• 100 molecules ke saath: 2¹⁰⁰
Aam formula: xʸ, jahan x = jagahon ki tadaad aur y = particles ki tadaad.

Diffusion is liye hota hai ke dono jars mein phailne par molecules ki tarteeb ke bohat se tareeqe ban jate hain. Particles ya un ki energy ki tarteeb ke tareeqon ka tasawwur batata hai ke koi tabdeeli ho sakti hai ya nahi.

blocks.prompt:
23 How can the entropies of substances be compared? State the rules for predicting the entropy change of a reaction, with two examples. (4 marks)
(Substances ki entropy ka muqabla kaise kiya jata hai? Reaction ke entropy change ka andaza lagane ke usool do misaalon ke saath bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Entropy ka muqabla:
• Particles ki tadaad: kam particles = kam entropy; CaCO₃ (92.9 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹) > CaO (39.7 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹).
• Sakhti (milti julti chemical fitrat): sakht substances ki kam entropy; diamond < graphite, kyun ke mazboot forces vibrations ko mehdood karti hain.
• Physical state: solid < liquid < gas; barf 48.0, paani 69.9, bhaap 188.7 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

Reaction ke usool (ΔS° positive jab):
1. Products mein solid liquid ya gas ban jaye.
2. Products ke moles zyada hon.
3. Gas molecules ki tadaad barhe (gases ki entropy zyada; zyada gas molecules, zyada tarteebein).

Misalein:
CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g): solid se gas banti hai, entropy barhti hai.
2N₂O₅(g) → 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g): 2 moles gas se 5 moles, entropy barhti hai.
Sirf positive ΔS spontaneity tay nahi karta: CaCO₃ ka tootna room temperature par spontaneous nahi.

24 Calculate ΔS°system for 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l), given S°[H₂(g)] = 130.6, S°[O₂(g)] = 205.0 and S°[H₂O(l)] = 69.9 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Explain the sign, and why the reaction can still be feasible. (4 marks)
(2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l) ka ΔS°system nikalein; S°[H₂(g)] = 130.6, S°[O₂(g)] = 205.0 aur S°[H₂O(l)] = 69.9 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Sign ki wajah batayein, aur yeh bhi ke reaction phir bhi kyun mumkin hai.)
blocks.explanation: ΔS°system = ΣnS°(products) – ΣnS°(reactants) lagayein, har S° ko us ke coefficient se zarb dein.

book_ref.quote: We know, however, that calcium reacts spontaneously with oxygen.

steps: Negative: 3 moles gas se liquid banta hai, is liye disorder kam hota hai. Reaction phir bhi mumkin hai kyun ke surroundings ki entropy bhi asar dalti hai; kul entropy change positive hona chahiye.
blocks.final_answer: ΔS°system = –326.4 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (system ki entropy kam hoti hai)

blocks.prompt:
25 What is Gibbs free energy? Derive the relation ΔG = ΔH – TΔS and explain how the sign of ΔG predicts the spontaneity of a process. (4 marks)
(Gibbs free energy kya hai? ΔG = ΔH – TΔS ka taaluq akhaz karein aur samjhayein ke ΔG ka sign process ki spontaneity kaise batata hai.)
blocks.explanation:
System ki heat content (enthalpy, H) do hisson par mushtamil hai:
• woh hissa jo doosri energy mein badal sakta hai, Gibbs free energy, G;
• woh hissa jo system ko us ke temperature par rakhne ke liye zaroori hai aur tabdeel nahi ho sakta, T × S.
H = G + TS
Is liye saari enthalpy sirf zero kelvin par dastyab hogi (TS = 0).

Akhaz: do halaton ke darmiyan tabdeeli ke liye,
ΔH = ΔG + Δ(TS)
Constant temperature par Δ(TS) = TΔS:
ΔH = ΔG + TΔS, yani ΔG = ΔH – TΔS (constant T)

ΔG ke sign se spontaneity:
• ΔG < 0 (–ve): process spontaneously ho sakta hai.
• ΔG > 0 (+ve): process khud nahi hota; ulta ho sakta hai.
• ΔG = 0: na process na ulta khud hota hai; system equilibrium mein hai.
Free energy ki zaroorat is liye hai ke kuch reactions mein sirf entropy change spontaneity nahi batata.

26 For 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l) at 25 °C, calculate ΔH°, ΔS° and ΔG° and discuss its spontaneity. Data: ΔH°f[H₂O(l)] = –286 kJ mol⁻¹; S°[H₂(g)] = 130.6, S°[O₂(g)] = 205.0, S°[H₂O(l)] = 69.9 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. (4 marks)
(25 °C par 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l) ke liye ΔH°, ΔS° aur ΔG° nikalein aur spontaneity par baat karein. Data: ΔH°f[H₂O(l)] = –286 kJ mol⁻¹; S°[H₂(g)] = 130.6, S°[O₂(g)] = 205.0, S°[H₂O(l)] = 69.9 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.)
blocks.explanation: Enthalpies of formation se ΔH° (elements = 0), standard entropies se ΔS°, ΔS° ko kJ K⁻¹ mein badlein, phir 298 K par ΔG° = ΔH° – TΔS°.

book_ref.quote: Also discuss its spontaneity.

steps: ΔG° negative hai, is liye reaction 25 °C par spontaneous hai, halan ke ΔS° negative hai; bara negative ΔH°, –TΔS° par bhaari hai.
blocks.final_answer: ΔH° = –572 kJ, ΔS° = –326.4 J K⁻¹, ΔG° = –474.7 kJ: 25 °C par spontaneous

blocks.prompt:
27 For CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g), ΔH° = +178 kJ mol⁻¹. Given S°[CaCO₃(s)] = 92.9, S°[CaO(s)] = 39.7 and S°[CO₂(g)] = 213.6 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, calculate ΔS° and ΔG° at 298 K, and the temperature above which the decomposition becomes spontaneous (take ΔH° and ΔS° as constant). (4 marks)
(CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g) ke liye ΔH° = +178 kJ mol⁻¹. S°[CaCO₃(s)] = 92.9, S°[CaO(s)] = 39.7 aur S°[CO₂(g)] = 213.6 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ le kar 298 K par ΔS° aur ΔG° nikalein, aur woh temperature jis se oopar tootna spontaneous ho jata hai (ΔH° aur ΔS° constant maan kar).)
blocks.explanation: ΔS° nikalein, phir ΔG° = ΔH° – TΔS°; reaction tab spontaneous hota hai jab TΔS°, ΔH° se barh jaye, yani T = ΔH°/ΔS° se oopar (jahan ΔG° = 0).

book_ref.quote: Quick Check 6.9 (b)(v) rightly treats limestone decomposing at room temperature as not spontaneous.

steps: ΔG°(298 K) = 178 – 298(0.1604) = 178 – 47.8 = +130.2 kJ mol⁻¹: positive, is liye room temperature par spontaneous nahi
Taqreeban 1110 K se oopar TΔS° > ΔH° aur ΔG° negative ho jata hai, is liye tootna spontaneous ho jata hai.
blocks.final_answer: ΔS° = +160.4 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; ΔG°(298 K) = +130.2 kJ mol⁻¹ (non-spontaneous); taqreeban 1110 K se oopar spontaneous

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Yeh sawal dikhata hai ke sirf positive ΔS kaafi nahi: kam temperature par +178 kJ ka ΔH haawi rehta hai, aur sirf zyada temperature par TΔS itna bara hota hai ke ΔG negative ho jaye.
